stemMd: A metal rod expands when heated. A circular hole in a thin plate of the same metal is heated uniformly without constraints. What happens to the hole?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Its diameter decreases because metal expands into the hole.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The hole disappears at any small temperature increase.

explanationMd: Imagine filling the hole with a disk of the same metal. Uniform heating would expand both the plate and the disk compatibly. Removing the imaginary disk leaves a larger hole. This geometric argument avoids the mistaken picture of material expanding only inward.

distractorRationale.a: Uniform expansion scales the whole plate pattern, including the hole.
distractorRationale.d: The hole boundary moves with the expanding material.
distractorRationale.b: Uniform isotropic expansion preserves the circular shape.
distractorRationale.c: Ordinary thermal expansion does not fill the hole.
